item.title: The type-A Hecke decomposition matrix is dominance unitriangular
item.statement: Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, $e=e(F,q)$ and $H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). For $\lambda\vdash n$ and $e$-regular $\mu\vdash n$ let $$d_{\lambda\mu}:=[S^{\lambda}:D^{\mu}],$$ the multiplicity of $D^{\mu}$ in a composition series of the Specht module $S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]). Then $$d_{\mu\mu}=1\qquad\text{and}\qquad d_{\lambda\mu}\ne0\ \Longrightarrow\ \mu\unrhd\lambda,$$ where $\unrhd$ is the dominance order on partitions ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]): a simple factor $D^{\mu}$ of $S^{\lambda}$ can occur only if the $e$-regular label $\mu$ dominates $\lambda$. Equivalently the decomposition matrix $(d_{\lambda\mu})$ is unitriangular along dominance. This constrains but does not compute the entries: no off-diagonal decomposition number is determined by cellularity.
item.strategy:
Apply [[cor-cellular-decomposition-matrices-are-dominance-unitriangular]] to the Murphy cellular basis ([[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]], [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]). In the source's dual normalisation it gives $d_{\lambda'
u'}
e0\Rightarrow\lambda'\unrhd
u'$, equivalently $
u'\unrhd\lambda'$, and transposition reverses dominance, giving $
u\unrhd\lambda$ for the Dipper-James labels used here (equivalently $\mu\unrhd\lambda$ for the simple label $\mu=
u'$). The diagonal value $d_{\mu\mu}=1$ is the diagonal statement of the cellular corollary. This is the translation of Mathas, Theorem 3.39(ii) to the page's convention, matching the group-side [[thm-symmetric-group-decomposition-matrix-is-dominance-unitriangular]]. No choice is used.

references.title: Mathas, Iwahori-Hecke Algebras and Schur Algebras of the Symmetric Group, Theorem 3.39(ii) with Corollary 2.14, printed pp. 13-16 and 34
G. D. James, The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups, Theorems 12.1-12.3 (dominance unitriangularity in the Dipper-James convention), printed pp. 42-43

item.title: The Hecke Jucys-Murphy action is dominance triangular
item.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, and let $L_1,\dots,L_n$ be the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements ([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]). For every $\lambda\vdash n$, every standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and every $1\le k\le n$ there exist $a_v\in R$ with $$m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_v\,m_v,$$ where $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ is the Murphy basis of the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) and the sum is over standard $\lambda$-tableaux $v$ strictly dominating $t$ in the dominance order on tableaux ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]], [[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). In particular $L_k$ acts on the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ with Murphy basis $(m_t)$ by a triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are the q-content values. Consequently the $L_k$ commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in $L_1,\dots,L_n$ is central in $H$.
item.strategy: Induct on $n$ and then on $k$ exactly as in the source. If $k$ lies in a non-last row of $t$, delete the last row and apply the induction hypothesis to the smaller partition; if $k$ is not in the first column, use $m_tL_k=m_t(1+L_{k-1}T_{k-1})$ together with the induction on $k$ and the quadratic relation; the remaining case (last row and first column) is handled by writing $m_t=hm_{\mu'}$ with $\mu'=(\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_r,1)$ and applying the Garnir relation Lemma 3.31 plus the induction hypothesis. The statement is for the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]), whose basis is $m_t=m_{t^\lambda t}$, so that the correction terms $m_{v^\lambda v}$ of the source's printed identity $m_{st}L_k=[\operatorname{res}_t(k)]_qm_{st}+\sum_{v\rhd t}r_vm_{sv}$ are the module basis vectors; the same triangularity in the Murphy-basis normalisation is [[Hu-Mathas]] Lemma 3.12 with (3.8). This is Mathas, Theorem 3.30 (Dipper-James) with Proposition 3.24 and Corollary 3.25. No choice is used.

item.title: Separated Hecke residues give seminormal idempotents and bases
item.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, let $e=e(F,q)$ and assume $e>n$ (with $e=\infty$ allowed); let $\lambda\vdash n$, $H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$, and let $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ be the Murphy cell module with Murphy basis $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]).
1. (**Separation**) If $s,t$ are standard $\lambda$-tableaux with $[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q$ for all $1\le k\le n$ then $s=t$. More precisely, if the q-content values agree for all $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$ for some $i$, then $s=t$ or $t=s(i\ i+1)$.
2. (**Idempotents**) For a standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ define, inside the commutative algebra $F[L_1,\dots,L_n]$, $$F_t:=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\ \prod_{\substack{s\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\\[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q\ne[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q}}\frac{L_k-[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q}{[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q-[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q}$$ and put $f_t:=m_tF_t\in S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$. All denominators are nonzero by (1) and the $f_t$ are well-defined spectral projectors: $f_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,f_t$, and $f_t=m_t+\sum_{s\rhd t}a_sm_s$ for suitable $a_s\in F$.
3. (**Orthogonal seminormal basis**) $\{f_t:t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is a basis of $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ satisfying $f_tF_s=\delta_{ts}f_t$ and $\langle f_s,f_t\rangle_\lambda=\delta_{st}\langle f_t,f_t\rangle_\lambda$; it is the **seminormal basis** of the Murphy cell module.
4. (**Generator action**) Let $s$ be a standard $\lambda$-tableau, $1\le i<n$ and $t:=s(i\ i+1)$, and put $\rho:=\operatorname{content}_s(i)-\operatorname{content}_s(i+1)\in\mathbb Z$ (an integer; it equals $\operatorname{res}_s(i)-\operatorname{res}_t(i)$ in the source's notation). If $i$ and $i+1$ lie in the same row of $s$ then $f_sT_i=q\,f_s$; if they lie in the same column then $f_sT_i=-f_s$; otherwise $t$ is standard and $$f_sT_i=\alpha_i(s)\,f_t-\frac{1}{[\rho]_q}f_s,\qquad \alpha_i(s):=\begin{cases}1,&s\rhd t,\\[1mm]\dfrac{[1+\rho]_q[1-\rho]_q}{[\rho]_q[-\rho]_q},&t\rhd s,\end{cases}$$ where $[-\rho]_q$ is the extended quantum integer of [[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]] and for the swapped tableau $\operatorname{content}_t(i)-\operatorname{content}_t(i+1)=-\rho$. No semisimplicity of $H$ is assumed and no choice principle is used.
item.strategy: (1) is Lemma 3.32: when $e>n$ the nodes of equal $e$-residue lie on diagonal lines, so distinct removable nodes have distinct residues, and peeling off $n,n-1,\dots,1$ determines $t$ from its q-content sequence. (2),(3) are Proposition 3.33 and Theorem 3.34: the triangularity of [[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] makes $F_t$ a projector annihilating strictly dominating tableaux; comparing $f_sL_k$ directly and using the associativity of the cellular form ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) gives $f_sF_t=\delta_{st}f_t$ and orthogonality. (4) is the coefficient computation of Theorem 3.34(ii): $f_sT_i$ is an eigenvector of every $L_k$ with $k\ne i,i+1$, so by (1) it lies in $\mathrm{span}(f_s,f_t)$; writing $f_sT_i=\alpha_i(s)f_t+c_sf_s$ and multiplying on the right by $L_i$ recovers $c_s=-1/[\rho]_q$ from the relation $T_iL_i=T_iL_{i+1}-1-(q-1)L_{i+1}$ of [[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]], and the quadratic relation $T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$ gives the product $\alpha_i(s)\alpha_i(t)=[1+\rho]_q[1-\rho]_q/([\rho]_q[-\rho]_q)$ for the swapped tableau $t$; since $\operatorname{content}_t(i)-\operatorname{content}_t(i+1)=-\rho$, the two standard cases have $\rho>0$ with $s\rhd t$ (branch $1$) and $\rho<0$ with $t\rhd s$ (branch $[1+\rho][1-\rho]/([\rho][-\rho])$). The stated branch assignment is the Mathas-Murphy seminormal coefficient system of Hu-Mathas (Example 3.11 with the axial distance (3.8), Lemma 3.12 and Proposition 3.17), which we verified directly in $H(S_3)$ ($\rho=2$, $q=3,5,7$) and $H(S_4)$ ($\rho=3$, $q=2$); the display of Theorem 3.34(ii) in the 1998 prepublication manuscript is inconsistent with the Hecke relations in the $t\rhd s$ case (exact computation in the batch notes), so the item uses the corrected form. The abstract cellular-algebra form of the same spectral construction is checked independently in Mathas-Soriano (separation condition, Proposition 4.13 and the appendix). No choice is used.

item.title: Hecke Specht theory specialises to group Specht theory at q = 1
item.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q=1\in F$, and let $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ be the specialization of the generic type-A Hecke algebra at $v\mapsto1$, so that $H_{F,1}(S_n)\cong F[S_n]$ with $T_w\mapsto w$ ([[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]]). Then the Hecke theory of this page specializes as follows.
1. The Murphy elements $m_\mu=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w$ specialize to the row symmetrizers $\sum_{w\in S_\mu}w$, and the Murphy basis $\{m_{st}\}$ of $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ specializes to the Murphy basis of the group algebra $F[S_n]$ (the base change $\mathbb Z[S_n]\to F[S_n]$ of the integral Murphy basis).
2. For every $\lambda\vdash n$ the specialization of the page's Hecke Specht module $S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) is the ordinary Specht module in the Dipper-James convention: $S^{\lambda}_{q=1}\cong S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ as $F[S_n]$-modules, with the standard polytabloid basis ([[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]); the specialized cell form is the standard bilinear form on $S^{\lambda}_k$ whose radical defines the James quotient $D^{\lambda}$ ([[def-modular-specht-form-and-radical-quotient]]).
3. The quantum characteristic of $q=1$ is $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)>0$, and $e=\infty$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)=0$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]); in characteristic $p>0$ a partition is $e$-regular exactly when it is $p$-regular. Hence $D^{\lambda}_{q=1}\ne0$ exactly for $p$-regular $\lambda$ ([[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]), and for non-$p$-regular $\lambda$ one has $\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}=S^{\lambda}$, so not every Specht module remains simple in characteristic $p$. This matches the group-side classification [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]] and the conjugate-sign dictionary [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]. In characteristic $0$ the specialization is split semisimple and all Specht modules are irreducible.
item.strategy: Base-change the Murphy cellular basis along $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to F$, $v\mapsto1$: the structure constants are polynomials in $q$, so specialization gives a cellular basis of $F[S_n]$, and the cell modules specialize to the modules with the specialized triangular multiplication. The identification with the Dipper-James Specht module uses the printed p. 25 convention warning of the source together with the conjugate-sign duality of [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]; the polytabloid/Murphy basis comparison is [[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]. The simple-label statement is the specialization of [[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]] at $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$, compared with [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]. The direction of information is one-way (this item imports the group classification and no group-side item depends on the Hecke theory). No choice is used.

references.title: Mathas, Iwahori-Hecke Algebras and Schur Algebras of the Symmetric Group, Chapter 1 sections 1-2 (specialization) and the p. 25 convention warning, printed pp. 3-6 and 25
Kleshchev, Symmetric groups and related Hecke algebras, Remark 5.5 and section 5.3 (the q=1, xi=1 case), p. 24

item.title: The Schur functor sends Weyl and simple modules to Specht and Hecke simple modules
item.strategy: By the definition of $\varphi_{ST}$, multiplying by $\varphi_{t^{\omega}t^{\omega}}$ kills all semistandard basis elements whose type is not $\omega$, and for type $\omega$ the surviving elements are exactly the $\varphi_t$ with $t$ a standard $\lambda$-tableau; this identifies the corner $W^{\lambda}e$ with the free module on the Murphy basis of the Hecke cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{M}}$, proving (1) for Weyl modules. Passing to heads and using that $F$ is exact ([[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]]) and sends the head of $W^{\lambda}$ to the head of $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{M}}$ gives $F(L^{\lambda})\cong D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{M}}$, which is nonzero exactly when $\lambda$ is $e$-restricted by Theorem 3.39, proving (2). Part (3) follows by applying the exact functor to a composition series of $W^{\lambda}$ and using (1)-(2) termwise, the multiplicities of the $D^{\nu}_{\mathrm{M}}$ with $\nu$ $e$-restricted being preserved. This is Mathas, Proposition 4.19 with the printed p. 25 convention warning; the Dipper-James translation is Kleshchev's Remark 5.5. No choice is used.

references.title: Mathas, Iwahori-Hecke Algebras and Schur Algebras of the Symmetric Group, Proposition 4.19 and its proof, printed pp. 43-44
Kleshchev, Symmetric groups and related Hecke algebras, Remark 5.5 (conjugation/sign dictionary), p. 24

item.title: Virtual Weyl and Specht symbols attached to beta sequences
item.strategy: A definition item assembled from the source's (5.21)-(5.22). The sorting sign is well defined because a strictly decreasing rearrangement is unique; the recovery formula is the inverse of $\nu'_i=b_i-n+i$, which produces a partition exactly in the non-vanishing case; and the recursion for $d_\mu$ on non-beta sequences is (5.22). In every use below either $b$ is the beta sequence of a partition or the displaced sequence is evaluated by Lemma 5.26, so no analytic assertion is smuggled into the definition. No choice is used.

item.title: The Jantzen filtration of a lifted cell module
item.statement: Let $R$ be a principal ideal domain ([[def-principal-ideal-domain]]) with a chosen prime element $\pi$, let $F:=R/\pi R$ be the residue field, and let $M$ be a free $R$-module of finite rank ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]) equipped with a symmetric $R$-bilinear form $\langle\ ,\ \rangle:M\times M\to R$ whose extension to the fraction field $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is non-degenerate (equivalently $\det G\ne0$ for a Gram matrix $G$ of the form). For $i\ge1$ put $$M(i):=\{x\in M:\langle x,y\rangle\in\pi^iR\ \text{for all }y\in M\},\qquad M_F(i):=(M(i)+\pi M)/\pi M\subseteq M_F:=M\otimes_RF.$$ Then $M(0)=M$, the $M(i)$ are $R$-submodules with $M(i+1)\subseteq M(i)$, the descending chain $$M_F=M_F(0)\supseteq M_F(1)\supseteq M_F(2)\supseteq\cdots$$ stabilises at $0$ (that is, $M_F(z)=0$ for all sufficiently large $z$, because $\det G\ne0$), and $M_F(1)=\mathrm{rad}\,M_F$, the radical of the reduced form. This finite descending filtration is the **Jantzen filtration** of $M$ with respect to $(R,\pi,\langle\ ,\ \rangle)$. The hypotheses are exactly: $R$ a PID, $\pi$ a prime element, the form non-degenerate over $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$; no valuation-ring or DVR hypothesis is substituted, and the prime element $\pi$, its ideal $\pi R$ and the fraction field $K$ are kept distinct.
item.strategy: A definition item. Each $M(i)$ is a submodule: for the cell forms on this page the associativity identity $\langle xa,y\rangle=\langle x,ya^*\rangle$ shows closedness under the action. Reduction gives a descending chain of finite-dimensional $F$-spaces, so it stabilises; $\det G\ne0$ makes the stable value $0$ because a vector whose pairing with every basis vector lies in all $\pi^iR$ is zero over $K$. Finally $x\in M(1)$ reduces into the radical of the reduced form by definition. This is Mathas, Chapter 5 section 2 (setup preceding Lemma 5.29), printed pp. 54-55; no choice is used.

references.title: Mathas, Iwahori-Hecke Algebras and Schur Algebras of the Symmetric Group, Chapter 5 section 2: the Jantzen filtration over a PID, printed pp. 54-55

item.title: The q-Schaper virtual radical-layer formula
item.statement:
Let $R$ be a principal ideal domain, $\pi$ a prime element, $F=R/\pi R$ the residue field, and let $\hat q\in R^{	imes}$ satisfy $[n]!_{\hat q}
e0$ in $R$; put $q:=\hat q+\pi R\in F^{	imes}$. Let $d\ge1$, let $\lambda$ be a partition of $n$ with at most $d$ parts, and let $W^{\lambda}_F$ be the Weyl module of the q-Schur algebra $S_F(d,n)=S(d,n)\otimes_RF$ with its Jantzen filtration $W^{\lambda}_F(i)$ with respect to $(R,\pi)$ ([[def-jantzen-filtration-of-a-lifted-cell-module]], [[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]).
1. (**Jantzen sum formula**) In the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional $S_F(d,n)$-modules, $$\sum_{i>0} igl[W^{\lambda}_F(i) igr]=\sum_{\substack{(a,b),(a,c)\in[\lambda]\ b<c}}\Bigl(
u_\pi igl([h^{\lambda}_{ab}]_{\hat q} igr)-
u_\pi igl([h^{\lambda}_{ac}]_{\hat q} igr)\Bigr)\Bigl[W_F^{( eta_1,\dots, eta_b+h^{\lambda}_{ab},\dots, eta_c-h^{\lambda}_{ac},\dots, eta_n)}\Bigr],$$ where $ eta= eta(\lambda)$ is the beta sequence of $\lambda$, $h^{\lambda}_{ab}$ are its hook lengths and the symbols are the virtual Weyl symbols of [[def-alternating-weyl-and-specht-symbols-from-beta-sequences]].
2. (**q-Schaper, $d\ge n$**) If $d\ge n$ and $\Pi$ denotes the Schur functor of [[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]], then applying $\Pi$ to (1) gives the corresponding identity for the Hecke Specht modules in the source's normalisation, that is, for the Murphy cell modules $\Pi(W^{\lambda}_F)=S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]] (the Dipper-James form is obtained by conjugating partitions), $$\sum_{i>0} igl[S^{\lambda}_F(i) igr]=\sum_{\substack{(a,b),(a,c)\in[\lambda]\ b<c}}\Bigl(
u_\pi igl([h^{\lambda}_{ab}]_{\hat q} igr)-
u_\pi igl([h^{\lambda}_{ac}]_{\hat q} igr)\Bigr)\Bigl[S_F^{( eta_1,\dots, eta_b+h^{\lambda}_{ab},\dots, eta_c-h^{\lambda}_{ac},\dots, eta_n)}\Bigr]$$ in the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional $H_{F,q}(S_n)$-modules, with the virtual Specht symbols of [[def-alternating-weyl-and-specht-symbols-from-beta-sequences]]. The formula is a virtual radical-layer identity: each nonzero coefficient bounds the corresponding composition multiplicity from above and forces at least one occurrence of the corresponding simple factor, but it is not a general algorithm for decomposition numbers.
item.strategy:
For (1): by [[thm-q-schur-weyl-weight-space-gram-determinant-hook-product]] the Gram determinant on the $
u$-weight space is a product of hook ratios times $q^{N}$; the assumption $[n]!_{\hat q}
e0$ (with $R$ a domain) makes every factor nonzero, and by Jantzen's lemma ([[lem-jantzen-layer-dimensions-equal-the-gram-determinant-valuation]]) its $\pi$-valuation equals the total dimension of the positive Jantzen layers on that weight space. Taking $\pi$-adic valuations of the hook product turns each factor into the difference $
u_\pi([h^{\lambda}_{ab}]_{\hat q})-
u_\pi([h^{\lambda}_{ac}]_{\hat q})$, and Lemma 5.26 identifies the index of each term with the virtual Weyl symbol $[W_F^{( eta_1,\dots, eta_b+h^{\lambda}_{ab},\dots, eta_c-h^{\lambda}_{ac},\dots, eta_n)}]$ (here the hook-to-removable-border-strip correspondence [[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]] is used). The resulting identities hold for every weight $
u$, so the unitriangular detection lemma [[lem-semistandard-weight-dimensions-detect-virtual-weyl-classes]] upgrades them to an identity in the Grothendieck group, giving (1). For (2) apply the exact Schur functor: by [[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]] it carries $W^{\lambda}_F(i)$ to $S^{\lambda}_F(i)$ and commutes with Grothendieck classes, so (1) transports termwise, the vanishing virtual symbols accounting for the zero terms. This is Mathas, Theorem 5.31 and Corollary 5.32 (q-Schaper), printed pp. 58-60; no choice is used.

references.title: Mathas, Iwahori-Hecke Algebras and Schur Algebras of the Symmetric Group, Theorem 5.31 (Jantzen sum formula) and Corollary 5.32 (q-Schaper theorem), printed pp. 58-60

item.title: The q-Schaper calculation for (3,2) at e = 2
item.statement:
Take $R=\mathbb C[\hat q]$, the prime element $\pi=1+\hat q$ (so that $F=\mathbb C$ and $q:=\hat q+\pi R$ specialises to $-1$, giving $e=2$), and $\lambda=(3,2)$, $n=5$. Evaluating the q-Schaper virtual sums ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]]) with the hook valuations $
u_\pi([2]_{\hat q})=
u_\pi([4]_{\hat q})=1$, $
u_\pi([3]_{\hat q})=
u_\pi([1]_{\hat q})=0$ gives, in the source's normalisation, $$\sum_{i>0} igl[W^{(3,2)}_F(i) igr]= igl[W^{(3,1^2)}_F igr]+ igl[W^{(2^2,1)}_F igr]- igl[W^{(1^5)}_F igr],\qquad \sum_{i>0} igl[S^{(3,2)}_F(i) igr]=2 igl[D^{(2^2,1)}_{\mathrm{M}} igr].$$ Further Jantzen calculations give $W^{(1^5)}_F=L^{(1^5)}_F$, $W^{(2^2,1)}_F=L^{(2^2,1)}_F$ and $W^{(3,1^2)}_F\sim L^{(3,1^2)}_F+L^{(2^2,1)}_F+L^{(1^5)}_F$, so at the level of the sum formula alone one gets $d_{(3,2),(3,1^2)}=1$ and only the bound $d_{(3,2),(2^2,1)}\in\{1,2\}$. The extra dimension/filtration argument on the Specht side gives $S^{(3,2)}_{\mathrm{M}}\cong D^{(2^2,1)}_{\mathrm{M}}$ (both sides have dimension $5$), whence $d_{(3,2),(2^2,1)}=1$: the virtual sum alone did not determine the entry. Translated to the Dipper-James convention of this page by conjugating and dualising ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]), this reads $S^{(2,2,1)}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong D^{(3,2)}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$, while the partition $(2,2,1)$ is not $2$-regular, so its own labelled head vanishes, $D^{(2,2,1)}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=0$. The computed entry is consistent with the dominance bound $d_{\lambda\mu}
e0\Rightarrow\mu\unrhd\lambda$ of [[cor-type-a-hecke-decomposition-matrix-is-dominance-unitriangular]].
item.strategy: Compute $\nu_\pi$ on the quantum hook lengths ($[k]_{\hat q}$ is divisible by $\pi=1+\hat q$ exactly when $k$ is even), use the evaluation of the $(3,2)$ Gram determinant displayed in Example 5.28, and read off the virtual sums; the small-module equalities and the final dimension count are Example 5.33 of the source, including its closing remark that $d_{(3,2),(2^2,1)}$ is determined only after the extra argument. The translation to the page's convention is the conjugate-dual dictionary of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]. No choice is used.

Kleshchev, Symmetric groups and related Hecke algebras, Remark 5.5 (label translation used for the restatement), p. 24

item.title: Cellularity does not make every cell module simple
item.statement: A cellular algebra need not be semisimple, its cell modules need not be simple, and a labelled head $D^{\lambda}$ may vanish although the cell module $C^{\lambda}$ is nonzero. (a) Abstract degenerate instance: let $F$ be a field and $A=F[x]/(x^2)$, with $\Lambda=\{1\rhd2\}$ ordered so that $1\rhd2$, cellular basis $c_{11}:=1$ in cell $1$ and $c_{22}:=x$ in cell $2$ and $i=\mathrm{id}$ ([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]). The triangular axiom holds because $1\cdot a\equiv0\bmod(x)$ for $a\in(x)$ and $x\cdot a\in\{x,0\}$, and $A^{\rhd2}=0$. The cell form on $C^{2}$ has $c_{22}c_{22}=x^2=0$, so it is identically zero, $\mathrm{rad}\,C^{2}=C^{2}$ and $D^{2}=0$, while $C^{1}\cong F$ is simple: cellularity does not force $D^{\lambda}\ne0$, and the algebra is not semisimple since $\mathrm{rad}\,A=(x)$. (b) Hecke instance: let $F$ be a field of characteristic $2$ and $q=1$, so $e=\operatorname{char}(F)=2$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]); for $n=3$ and $\lambda=(1,1,1)$ the partition $(1,1,1)$ is not $2$-regular ([[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]]), so $D^{(1,1,1)}=0$ while the page's Specht module $S^{(1,1,1)}\cong D^{(3)}$ is the nonzero trivial module (in characteristic $2$ the sign module is trivial) ([[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]], [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]). (c) Reducible cell module: at $e=2$ the q-Schur cell module $W^{(3,2)}_F$ satisfies $\sum_{i>0}[W^{(3,2)}_F(i)]=[L^{(3,1^2)}_F]+2[L^{(2^2,1)}_F]\ne0$ ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]], the calculation of [[ex-q-schaper-for-shape-three-two-at-e-two]]), so its radical is nonzero and $W^{(3,2)}_F$ is reducible even though it has a simple head.
item.strategy: Part (a) is a direct computation in the two-dimensional algebra $F[x]/(x^2)$: every product of two elements of the smaller cell vanishes. Part (b) reads the $2$-regularity of $(1,1,1)$ off the definition and applies the classification theorem; the cell module $S^{(1^3)}$ at $q=1$ is the sign module, which is the trivial module in characteristic $2$. Part (c) is the Weyl-module computation of Example 5.33, where the Jantzen layers have positive dimension. All three instances are applications of [[thm-nonzero-cell-heads-classify-the-simple-modules-of-a-cellular-algebra]], whose third clause says that $D^{\lambda}\ne0$ holds exactly when the cell form is non-degenerate. No choice is used.

Mathas-Soriano, Seminormal forms and Gram determinants for cellular algebras, sections 3.1-3.7 (degenerate cell forms), pp. 9-11

item.title: Type-A Hecke Specht modules are in the same block iff their labels have the same e-core
item.statement: Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e$, and let $S^{\lambda}$ be the type-A Hecke Specht module of this page in the Dipper-James convention ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) for $\lambda\vdash n$. Then for all partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ the modules $S^{\lambda}$ and $S^{\mu}$ lie in the same block of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Equivalently the blocks of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ are indexed by the $e$-cores $\gamma$ of size at most $n$ with $|\gamma|\equiv n\pmod e$, and the block of $S^{\lambda}$ is determined by $C_e(\lambda)$. (For $e=\infty$ the Hecke algebra is semisimple and each partition is its own core, so the statement is the trivial block decomposition.)

item.title: Weight-one block decomposition pattern
item.statement: Let $e\ge2$, let $\gamma$ be an $e$-core of $m$, and put $n=m+e$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). There are exactly $e$ partitions $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$ of $n$ with $e$-core $\gamma$; list them in dominance order, $\lambda_1\rhd\lambda_2\rhd\cdots\rhd\lambda_e$. In the source's (Murphy/dual-Specht) normalisation the Weyl modules and simple modules of this block satisfy $W^{\lambda_e}=L^{\lambda_e}$ and $[W^{\lambda_k}]=[L^{\lambda_k}]+[L^{\lambda_{k+1}}]$ for $1\le k<e$, so the decomposition matrix is the $e\times e$ bidiagonal matrix with rows and columns $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$; and exactly $\lambda_1$ is not $e$-restricted while $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_e$ are. Under the Schur functor ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]) the corresponding Murphy Specht classes are $[S^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]$, $[S^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]+[D^{\lambda_{k+1}}_{\mathrm M}]$ for $2\le k<e$ and $[S^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}]$, with $D^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}=0$; conjugating partitions and dualising ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]) gives the corresponding decomposition matrix for the page's Dipper-James Specht modules in $e$-regular labels.
item.strategy: The abacus of [[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]] shows that the partitions of $n=m+e$ with $e$-core $\gamma$ are obtained from $\gamma$ by moving one bead up one row on one runner, so there are exactly $e$ of them; ordered by dominance they are $\lambda_1\rhd\cdots\rhd\lambda_e$, with $\lambda_e$ the one whose bead has the lowest target position and $\lambda_1$ the one obtained by adjoining all $e$ boxes to the first row. For each $k$ the Jantzen sum formula of [[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]] evaluates in this weight-one configuration to $\sum_{i>0}[W^{\lambda_k}_F(i)]\sim\sum_{j>k}(-1)^{j-k+1}[W^{\lambda_j}_F]$, because the only nonzero hook valuations are the consecutive ones; the resulting triangular system, with the simple modules detected through [[lem-virtual-weyl-combinations-detect-q-schur-block-separation]] and the block classification, has the unique solution $[W^{\lambda_k}]=[L^{\lambda_k}]+[L^{\lambda_{k+1}}]$ for $k<e$ and $W^{\lambda_e}=L^{\lambda_e}$. The $e$-restricted pattern follows from $D^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}=0$, which is exactly the non-$e$-restricted vanishing of the cell head, together with $F(W^{\lambda_1})=F(L^{\lambda_2})$ and the Schur-functor dictionary; the Dipper-James translation is the conjugation/duality dictionary of the Specht-module definition. This is Mathas, Proposition 5.38 with its printed Jantzen computation, printed pp. 61-63; the numeric pattern is worked out again in this pair's examples companion. No choice principle is used.

item.title: The nondegenerate root-of-unity level-one Hecke regime
item.statement:
**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP) $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written $\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]].

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$ is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]), and $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks ([[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the same $e$ and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ ([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series ([[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]); a different series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus $\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter, equal to the source's $\xi$) and $q$ (the grading variable, equal to the source's quantum variable) are INDEPENDENT data; the design's phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of a square $q_{\rm src}^2$, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model $\mathcal F_{\rm sym}$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge $0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$, basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$, empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ let $\lambda'$ be the conjugate, which is $e$-regular and labels the Hecke simple module in the Dipper-James convention of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]; at $e=p$ prime and $\xi=1$ this is the published [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]].

No choice principle is used.
item.strategy: Direct convention check. At level one $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i,0}$, so the cyclotomic polynomial of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] is $\prod_i(X_1-\xi^i)^{(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)}=X_1-1$ and the KLR cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$; the finite-characteristic hypothesis $e\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ makes $\xi\ne1$ a primitive $e$-th root, and in sub-branch (CP) the hypothesis $p\nmid e$ is exactly what makes a primitive $e$-th root exist in $F$. The type-$A$ datum and the grading are batch-24 clauses; the transport statement is the graded block isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] with [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock-side residues, the restricted labels and the empty component are batch-9/batch-23 clauses. The dictionary to the $e$-regular Dipper-James labels is the recorded convention of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]] together with the published conjugate-sign proposition; for the Hecke side with general finite $e$ no prime-field statement is inferred, since that proposition is stated for $k[S_n]$ in characteristic $p$. The parameter dictionary is the naming clause of [BK 2009 §1 and §4.2] and [Ariki 1996 §1]; it makes no substitution. No choice is used.

item.title: A graded algebra isomorphism transports the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups and its dualities
item.statement:
Let $\rho:R\to H$ be an isomorphism of finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras. Restriction of scalars along $\rho$ is an equivalence of graded left module categories which is exact, sends finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, sends a shift $M\{r\}$ to $M\{r\}$, sends finitely generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives, preserves composition multiplicities of graded simples (with shifts), and identifies the graded Hom pairings $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}$ of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]. It therefore induces $A$-module isomorphisms $K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to K_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ and $G_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ intertwining the Cartan homomorphisms and the forgetful maps $\zeta$.

If moreover $\rho$ intertwines fixed anti-automorphisms $\ast_R$ and $\ast_H$ (i.e. $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$), then the transported functor intertwines the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ and the two projective Hom-dualities $\#$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], and hence preserves normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives.

**Application.** For every residue content $\alpha$ with $e_\alpha\ne0$, the Brundan-Kleshchev isomorphism $\rho_\alpha:R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] with the transported grading of [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]] intertwines the descended anti-involutions: on the explicit Khovanov-Lauda generators the transported Hecke anti-involution induced by $\rho_\alpha$ fixes $e(i)$ and $y_r$ and sends the crossing $\psi_r$ to the element (3.32)/(4.37) of the source, all of whose ingredients are fixed. Consequently all conclusions apply blockwise to $\rho_\alpha$; this transported duality is the normalization used for the Hecke-side modules below, and no comparison with the coarser ungraded cellular duality of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]] is claimed.
item.strategy: Restriction of scalars along an isomorphism is an equivalence; exactness and the module-level properties are immediate from the functor $M\mapsto M$ with action $x\cdot m=\rho(x)m$. Shifts are preserved because $\rho$ is degree-preserving. Fitting decomposition/projectivity: a retract of $H^{\oplus n}$ pulls back to a retract of $R^{\oplus n}$. Composition multiplicities and graded Hom dimensions agree because the functor is an isomorphism of categories fixing Hom spaces up to the identity-on-underlying-sets identification. The Grothendieck conclusions follow from exactness and split-exactness. The duality clause is a direct computation: $(D_\psi M)(f)$ versus the transported functional, using $\rho\ast_R=\ast_H\rho$; the projective $\#$ duality is the same computation on $\operatorname{HOM}(P,R)$. For the application, verify the intertwining on generators: the Hecke anti-involution is the transported KLR one by construction of the isomorphism, and the source formulas [BK4 §3.2 (3.31)-(3.32) and §4.4 (4.36)-(4.37)] express $y_re(i)$ and $\psi_re(i)$ through fixed generators of the affine Hecke algebra (idempotents, dots and simple transpositions), so it fixes them; since the $e(i),y_r,\psi_r$ generate, the two anti-involutions correspond. No choice.

item.title: The graded Specht module by homogeneous standard tableaux
item.statement:
Work in the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. Fix a partition $\mu$, put $d=|\mu|$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $K(\mu)$ be the $F$-span of the Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] with $S,T$ standard tableaux of a multipartition strictly dominating $\mu$; by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] $K(\mu)$ is a two-sided ideal of $H^\Lambda_d$ and $z_\mu:=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is defined. Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module** $$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$ a right $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$ fix a reduced decomposition $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put $z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov-Lauda presentation of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]. For a removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$ define $d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$ (equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by $\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$, $\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing $d$.

The definition asserts, and proves below in [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of $S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_T q^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** $S(\mu)$ is the cell module of the Dipper-James-Mathas cellular structure; it is the DUAL of the module called Specht module in [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]. Consequently the restricted (respectively $e$-regular) labels belong to $S(\mu)$ with $\mu$ restricted (respectively conjugate $e$-regular) in the convention of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]] and [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]; no statement about $S(\mu)$ is silently transferred to the other convention. The labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

No choice is used in the definition.
item.strategy: This is a definition with its construction; the asserted basis, homogeneity and module structure are discharged by [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], and the ideal/cellular facts by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]]. The degree recursion is the source's (4.33); the vectors $v_T$ depend a priori on the chosen reduced decompositions, and the theorem proves the resulting grading is well defined. The dictionary to [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]] is recorded as a convention, exactly as the source records that its $S(\mu)$ is the dual of the older Specht module [BKW §4.1]. No choice.
